Knitting a sweater is really just tying an incredibly complicated knot.

It's actually very similar to certain kinds of sinnets, known as "chain sinnet," in which you make a loop in the yarn and push a loop through that loop, and then push another loop through that loop, and so on.

Why yes, I am a huge knot nerd, thanks for asking.

Edit: Oh, shit, I forgot to explain "sinnet." A sinnet is a kind of knot that basically turns into a cord of sorts as you keep going and you can make it to any length you need.
I might be nit picking, but what you are describing is similar to crocheting not knitting.

Well, yes, that is true - I mean, a simple chain sinnet is literally the same as a "chain stitch" in crochet, after all...

But on the other hand, to my mind, crochet, knitting, and chain sinnets are all theoretically very similar. If you've got nimble fingers and a bit of time to figure it out, it's possible to do a chain sinnet with two loops instead of just one, and then from there, you can do three, four, or more. The only difference between that and a knit sock is just how big around the circle is and the method you use to make it - the course of the yarn or cord through the finished item will look the same.
